newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia sees $4-5 bln foreign investment in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Russia sees $4-5 bln foreign investment in 1997.

text.p: Russia expects foreign investment to rise to $4-5 billion this year from $2.5-3.0 billion in 1996, economy minister Yevgeny Yasin told a news conference.
"We had foreign investment of about $2.5-3.0 billion last year excluding state Treasury bills. This year we can expect between $4 and $5 billion," he said.
Yasin, discussing Russia's economic performance in 1996, said the country was moving towards economic growth.
"Financial stability was basically achieved and we can move on to the economic growth. But the present stage between stability and growth is the most difficult," he said.
Interfax news agency quoted Yasin as saying Russia could have economic growth of five percent by 2000 and between eight and nine percent by 2005.
Russian 1996 gross domestic product fell by six percent on the previous year's levels.
